<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Reuse the existing SSE data-field extractor in the Python completions, chat-completions, and audio benchmark clients, so valid event metadata and comments do not turn successful responses into failed benchmark requests.

## Claims

- Accept metadata/comment lines, `data:` without an optional space, and multiline JSON data within each message emitted by the existing stream handler, in all three streaming clients.
- Ignore events without a nonempty data payload while continuing to fail on malformed JSON in the extracted payload. See the existing framing limitation below.
- Preserve generated text (including Unicode line separators), token accounting, and existing timing behavior; no model or kernel changes.

## Validation

Validated on macOS / Apple M4 CPU with Python 3.12.13 and Torch 2.14.0. Baseline: `405276b8f0354ddf8686aa5da2f905e76427f1a8`, with the new tests present and the production module unchanged.

| Check | Before fix | After fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 21 local HTTP SSE cases across completions/chat/audio | 15 failed, 6 passed | 21 passed within the suite below |
| Real `RemoteOpenAIServer` regression | Failed with `JSONDecodeError` | Passed; exact text and token usage match direct reference |
| Server regression + timing + Responses suites | Not run as a combined baseline | 84 passed, 3 warnings in 21.15s |

The server test loads real `facebook/opt-125m` weights (cached revision `27dcfa74d334bc871f3234de431e71c6eeba5dd6`), using float32, eager execution, a 256-token context, one sequence, 128 MiB KV cache, greedy sampling, and seed 0. A forwarding proxy prepends `event`/`id`/`retry`/comment fields to the actual generated stream. The benchmark result must match the direct nonstreaming OpenAI-client reference, including all 8 output tokens and prompt usage.

<details>
<summary>Commands and baseline failure evidence</summary>

Before the fix (new tests present, production module verified identical to the baseline):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py \
  -k extract_sse_payload --tb=line -q
# 15 failed, 6 passed, 38 deselected in 1.00s

env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 \
  VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=nobind VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/benchmarks/test_serve_cli.py::test_bench_serve_sse_metadata \
  --tb=short -q
# 1 failed, 3 warnings in 18.95s
```

Relevant baseline output from the real server test:

```text
tests/benchmarks/test_serve_cli.py:87: in test_bench_serve_sse_metadata
    assert output.success, output.error
    ... async_request_openai_completions ...
        data = json.loads(chunk)
json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
```

After the fix:

```bash
env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 \
  VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=nobind VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/benchmarks/test_serve_cli.py::test_bench_serve_sse_metadata \
  tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py \
  tests/benchmarks/test_responses_request_func.py --tb=short -q
# 84 passed, 3 warnings in 21.15s

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  tests/benchmarks/test_serve_cli.py \
  tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py \
  vllm/benchmarks/lib/endpoint_request_func.py \
  docs/benchmarking/cli.md
# All applicable hooks passed, including mypy and test-tethering.

git diff --check
# Passed.
```

The warnings are pre-existing unregistered `pytest.mark.benchmark` markers. The existing Buildkite Benchmarks CLI step selects these tests and covers the changed source paths. GPU execution, audio-model end-to-end validation, model accuracy/performance benchmarks, the full benchmark suite, and a rendered docs build were not run. No speedup or GPU-validation claim is made.

</details>

## Details

The three clients previously stripped only a leading literal `data: ` prefix. Other SSE fields therefore reached `json.loads`, while skipping whole messages starting with `:` could discard valid data following a comment. This change reuses `_extract_sse_data`, already used by the Responses client, without changing its implementation or the shared stream-framing handler. Documentation is updated under Online Benchmark.

Duplicate checks found no matching open Python payload-extraction fix. Related work is distinct: #61534 and #61576 modify stream framing; #57519 detects error objects inside JSON payloads; #60177 changes the Rust benchmark client. This patch does not modify any of those mechanisms.

Known framing limitation, raised in [this review comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64143#issuecomment-6456047182): the existing handler can emit a complete JSON value before the event's blank-line delimiter. A single event containing two separate JSON values on two `data:` lines fails JSON parsing when delivered together, but can be processed as two messages if an HTTP chunk ends immediately after the first value. This was reproduced locally at the real handler/extractor level, and the handler's AST is identical between the tested baseline and `78b9199`. Strict multiline-event validation across arbitrary chunk boundaries is not claimed or fixed here. The benchmark documentation now records this limitation; framing remains outside this patch's scope.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex helped author and review the patch and tests and prepare this description. The submitter confirmed code review and directed Codex to execute the tests on their Mac and publish after they passed. The validation commands reported here were executed by Codex, not manually by the submitter.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

Independently checked `78b9199` on Linux: the metadata fix works for completions and chat. One pre-existing framing caveat to the malformed-JSON claim:

```text
data: {"choices":[{"text":"A"}]}
data: {"choices":[{"text":"B"}]}

```

This is one SSE event; joining its data fields with a newline does not produce a single valid JSON value. Sending it in one HTTP write correctly produces `JSONDecodeError`. Sending the exact same bytes in two writes, split immediately after the first `}` and before the single newline, returns `success=True` and text `AB` instead. A normal usage event and `[DONE]` follow in both cases.

I reproduced both outcomes through the actual completions/chat request functions and an aiohttp loopback server. Observing the real handler calls confirms that the first JSON is emitted before the event delimiter arrives. Independently delimited events and a split UTF-8 character are healthy controls.

The same behavior exists at base `4d95f222`, so this is **not a regression from this PR**. Since #61534/#61576 already cover framing work, this may be best recorded there or kept as an explicit limitation rather than expanding this payload-extraction patch.

Scope: exact complete request module, Python 3.12.10, aiohttp 3.14.5; not a full vLLM build, audio/model test or official CI.

Thanks for independently checking this and for the precise reproducer. Confirmed locally at the real `StreamedResponseHandler` / `_extract_sse_data` level: delivering both data lines together raises `JSONDecodeError`, while splitting immediately after the first JSON value emits two messages and produces `AB`. Independently delimited events remain a healthy control. The handler AST is unchanged between our tested baseline (`405276b8`) and `78b9199`.

Updated the PR claims and added the explicit framing limitation to `docs/benchmarking/cli.md` in a4a0dfe. This follow-up changes documentation only; strict event-boundary validation remains outside this payload-extraction patch. No framing changes are included.

Re-ran the real CPU server regression plus the timing/Responses suites: **84 passed, 3 pre-existing marker warnings (21.15s)**. Documentation pre-commit checks also passed.

Checked the change against main. With `event:`/`id:` lines ahead of `data:`, the handler's early-emit branch doesn't fire (it needs the buffer to start with `data: `), so those messages wait for the blank line and reach `_extract_sse_data` whole. The three clients now parse the same way the Responses client does.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Checked the change against main. With `event:`/`id:` lines ahead of `data:`, the handler's early-emit branch doesn't fire (it needs the buffer to start with `data: `), so those messages wait for the blank line and reach `_extract_sse_data` whole. The three clients now parse the same way the Responses client does.

This starts a second model server in the Benchmarks CI step. vLLM's server never sends `event:`, `id:` or `retry:` on completions, so the proxy injects them, which is what the local HTTP server in `test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py` already does for all three clients. I don't think the real model adds coverage here. Could this test be dropped?

 ### 🚀 Online Benchmark
 
+The Python `vllm bench serve` client accepts SSE comments, `event:`, `id:`, and

+The stream handler retains early JSON emission: if an HTTP chunk ends after a

Independently checked `78b9199` on Linux: the metadata fix works for completions and chat. One pre-existing framing caveat to the malformed-JSON claim:

```text
data: {"choices":[{"text":"A"}]}
data: {"choices":[{"text":"B"}]}

```

This is one SSE event; joining its data fields with a newline does not produce a single valid JSON value. Sending it in one HTTP write correctly produces `JSONDecodeError`. Sending the exact same bytes in two writes, split immediately after the first `}` and before the single newline, returns `success=True` and text `AB` instead. A normal usage event and `[DONE]` follow in both cases.

I reproduced both outcomes through the actual completions/chat request functions and an aiohttp loopback server. Observing the real handler calls confirms that the first JSON is emitted before the event delimiter arrives. Independently delimited events and a split UTF-8 character are healthy controls.

The same behavior exists at base `4d95f222`, so this is **not a regression from this PR**. Since #61534/#61576 already cover framing work, this may be best recorded there or kept as an explicit limitation rather than expanding this payload-extraction patch.

Scope: exact complete request module, Python 3.12.10, aiohttp 3.14.5; not a full vLLM build, audio/model test or official CI.

Thanks for independently checking this and for the precise reproducer. Confirmed locally at the real `StreamedResponseHandler` / `_extract_sse_data` level: delivering both data lines together raises `JSONDecodeError`, while splitting immediately after the first JSON value emits two messages and produces `AB`. Independently delimited events remain a healthy control. The handler AST is unchanged between our tested baseline (`405276b8`) and `78b9199`.

Updated the PR claims and added the explicit framing limitation to `docs/benchmarking/cli.md` in a4a0dfe. This follow-up changes documentation only; strict event-boundary validation remains outside this payload-extraction patch. No framing changes are included.

Re-ran the real CPU server regression plus the timing/Responses suites: **84 passed, 3 pre-existing marker warnings (21.15s)**. Documentation pre-commit checks also passed.

Checked the change against main. With `event:`/`id:` lines ahead of `data:`, the handler's early-emit branch doesn't fire (it needs the buffer to start with `data: `), so those messages wait for the blank line and reach `_extract_sse_data` whole. The three clients now parse the same way the Responses client does.
